activities.title: Sort by first sound
materials: small objects or pictures that start with two different sounds, such as sock and moon
parentPrompts: Pick two sounds, such as /s/ and /m/. Put one object for each sound in separate spots to start.
Hold up an object, say its name, and stretch the first sound. Ask them to put it with the matching group.
Say the sound before each object: "Does moon start with sss or mmm?"
Let them find new objects around the house for each group.

activities.title: Clap helper words
parentPrompts: Say each helper word and clap its parts: doc-tor (2), po-lice (2), fire-fight-er (3), teach-er (2), nurse (1).
Ask: "How many claps for fire-fighter?"
Ask what each helper does, and clap their names again.
Let them pick a helper for you to clap.

activities.title: Alphabet song and pointing
parentPrompts: Sing the alphabet song together while you point to each letter on the chart.
Slow down and stop at a letter. Ask: "What letter is this?"
Find the letters of their name on the chart and point to each one.
Pick one letter to look for today on signs, boxes, and books.

activities.title: Rhymes with helper words
parentPrompts: Say a pair of rhymes: nurse and purse, mail and snail, truck and duck. Ask: "Do they sound the same at the end?"
Say three words and ask which one does not rhyme, like "mail, snail, dog."
Make up silly rhymes for helper words: "doctor, mocktor."
Take turns making up your own rhyming pairs.

activities.title: Read about helpers
materials: a picture book about community helpers
parentPrompts: Read the book together. Ask: "Who is this helper? How do they help people?"
After reading, ask them to retell the story: "What happened first? Then what? How did it end?"
Ask: "Which helper would you like to be?"
Talk about someone who helps your family, such as a neighbor or a teacher.

activities.title: Morning, afternoon, night
parentPrompts: Draw or talk about three parts of the day: morning, afternoon, and night. Ask: "What do we do in the morning?"
Put pictures or drawings of daily activities in order: wake up, lunch, bath, bedtime.
Use time words: first, next, later, today, yesterday, tomorrow. Ask: "What will we do tomorrow?"
Ask: "What happens before bed? What happens after breakfast?"

activities.title: Longer or shorter?
materials: a spoon, a crayon, a shoe, a book, and other household objects
parentPrompts: Line up two objects with their ends together at the same starting line. Ask: "Which is longer? Which is shorter?"
Try different pairs. Ask them to predict first, then check.
Find something longer than a shoe and something shorter than a crayon.
Line up three objects from shortest to longest.

activities.title: Which holds more?
materials: a few cups and bowls of different sizes
parentPrompts: Stay with your child during water play. Use a tub or a sink with just a little water, or use dry rice.
Fill a small cup and pour it into a big bowl. Ask: "Does the bowl hold more or less than the cup?"
Ask them to guess which container holds the most, then test it by pouring.
Line up the containers from holds-the-least to holds-the-most.

activities.title: Heavy or light?
materials: a few objects of different weights, such as a book, a feather, a rock, and a sock
parentPrompts: Hold two objects, one in each hand, and ask: "Which is heavier? Which is lighter?"
Let them hold them and guess. Then compare with a homemade balance if you like: a hanger with a small bag on each end.
Predict first: "Do you think the book is heavier than the sock?"
Find something in the house that is heavy and something that is light.

activities.title: Join and take away
materials: up to 5 small toys, such as toy cars
parentPrompts: Put 2 cars on the table. Add 1 more car and say: "2 cars and 1 more car. How many cars now?" Count to check.
Take one car away: "I have 3 cars. One drives away. How many are left?"
Tell a little story with each problem, like "Two cars were parked. One more car came."
Stay with 5 or fewer, and let them move the toys themselves.

activities.title: Draw my day
parentPrompts: Fold the paper into three parts. Label them morning, afternoon, and night, or have your child help.
Ask them to draw what they do in each part of the day.
Ask them to tell you about each picture, and write what they say underneath.
Use the words first, next, and last as they talk.

activities.title: Helper hats
parentPrompts: Make a paper hat, such as a firefighter helmet or a chef hat. An adult can do the taping or stapling.
Let them decorate it.
Put on the hat and pretend to be that helper. Ask: "How do you help people?"
Take turns, and be the person who needs help.

activities.title: Build a town
parentPrompts: Build a town together out of boxes and blocks: a school, a store, a fire station.
Ask: "What places are in our town? Who works there?"
Use toy cars and people for pretend play.
Let them describe their town to you like a tour guide.

activities.title: Thank-you card for a helper
parentPrompts: Choose a helper to thank, such as a mail carrier, teacher, neighbor, or doctor.
Fold a paper in half. Let them draw a picture on the front.
Write the words they say inside: "Thank you for helping." Let them write their name or a mark.
Deliver it together.

activities.title: Make a shaker
materials: a small plastic bottle with a cap
parentPrompts: An adult puts a spoonful of rice in the bottle and tapes the cap on tightly. Keep it away from mouths, and check the tape.
Let them decorate the outside with markers or stickers.
Shake along to music: fast, slow, loud, and quiet.
Play stop and go: shake when the music plays, freeze when it stops.
